rubric.notes: Not run by design: make test/golden (CLAUDE.md Merges). AC1/AC2 fresh-clone Godot SCRIPT ERROR count UNMEASURED by me (optional, skipped); executor's V6 claim not independently reproduced.

findings.summary: The make test and make golden bounds have no hang case; unbounding either survives the control.
findings.evidence: Mutants X3 (bounded "$TEST_S" make test -> make test) and X4 (same for golden) both left the control at 16 cases, 0 failures, rc 0. Only deps, sky-assets and runtime have hang cases. The doc says every make call is bounded, but 2 of 6 are unguarded by tests.

findings.summary: The TERM-to-KILL escalation is untested: the stub hang child (sleep) dies on TERM.
findings.evidence: Mutant X2 (delete kill KILL, -$pid) survives, rc 0, 16 cases 0 failures. A child that traps TERM would hang bounded forever in waitpid.

findings.summary: bounded signals only the process group of the direct child; a process that setsid()s or leaves the group is missed. If the leader exits normally, surviving group members are not reaped, so the EXIT trap rm -rf can race them.
findings.evidence: Read of bounded: the normal path is waitpid then exit with no kill -0 -pid sweep. Timeout path always TERM, sleep 2, KILL the group then waitpid, so the race is closed only there. Also waitpid after KILL could block on an uninterruptible child, and RIG_*_S=0 disables the alarm. Practical risk low.

findings.summary: Interrupting rig_check.sh itself (INT/TERM to the sh) does not run the EXIT trap or signal an active bounded group.
findings.evidence: Pre-existing behaviour; bounded handles signals sent to perl only. Not introduced here, noted for completeness.
